subject: Urgent: P95/P99 spike after A/B variant B rollout — request for rollback
messages:
From: John Diaz <john.diaz@stardata.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — immediate performance impact

Vanessa,

We kicked off the A/B rollout this morning (variant B to 25% traffic) and are seeing a steep jump in p95 and p99 on our integrated endpoints. Error rate is still low but tail latency is spiking for some customer flows — notably content generation and batch summarization. Our SRE alerted us at 09:05 PST with a ~3x p99 increase.

Can Redwood pause variant B or route the affected customers back to variant A while you triage? This is customer-facing and customers are already complaining about slow responses.

Attached are our Datadog snapshots. Please treat as urgent.

— John
Head of Platform, Stardata

Attachments: dd-screens-09-05.png (image/png)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: John Diaz <john.diaz@stardata.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — immediate performance impact

John — thanks for the heads up and sorry you hit this. We are escalating immediately.

Marcus and team — tagging you to triage. Can you confirm whether the spike correlates with variant B path (model v2.1-q4f) and whether there are any changes to batching/quantization kernels that could cause tail amplification? If we can pause variant B or shift traffic back to variant A (v2.0-q8), please advise recommended action and ETA.

I will update Stardata in 15 minutes with an interim status.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — initial triage notes

On Mon, 29 Apr 2029 at 09:21, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai wrote:
> Marcus and team — tagging you to triage.

Quick triage summary (interim):
- Correlation: yes, p95/p99 increase aligns with the start of variant B at ~08:58 PT. Canary injected at 25% traffic.
- Symptoms: tail latency increase (p99 ~ 3x), CPU skew on host pool serving variant B, higher queuing at the batching gateway for sequences >1024 tokens. Error rates unchanged.
- Suspected cause: kernel/codepath for the quantized model v2.1-q4f introduces a slower attention kernel when sequence-length distribution skews long; also fallback to CPU for a small subset of requests observed in profiling.

Immediate recommended actions (we can execute in ~10–20 min):
1) Pause variant B rollout (stop new canary allocations) and drain existing B sessions to completion (recommended) OR
2) Route B traffic to region/dedicated nodes with larger batch capacity (more complex) OR
3) Roll back traffic for customers showing degradation to variant A.

I've uploaded quick profiles and the canary metrics to the shared folder and attached dd-profiles and canary CSV export. Marcus

Attachments: dd-profiles-20290429.txt; canary-metrics-variantB-20290429.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: John Diaz <john.diaz@stardata.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — Redwood action plan (interim)

John — interim update and proposed mitigation: 

We have confirmed the p95/p99 regression is associated with the variant B model (v2.1-q4f) in our hosted inference pool. Our engineering lead recommends pausing the canary and draining current B requests to avoid in-flight interruptions.

Proposed immediate steps (we can apply now if you approve):
- Pause further canary traffic to variant B and set routing to variant A for all customer traffic (this is a non-disruptive routing change).
- Continue profiling variant B in a separate pool to identify the attention kernel fallback and batching pathology.
- We will provide an executive summary and concrete rollback playbook within 90 minutes.

Do we have permission to flip traffic back to variant A now? If yes, we will execute and confirm when p99 returns to baseline.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: John Diaz <john.diaz@stardata.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@stardata.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — approve rollback

Vanessa — please proceed with the rollback to variant A and keep us posted. Customers are seeing timeouts on long-run jobs; we prefer a safe rollback. Feel free to reach out if you need any logs from our side.

— John

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: John Diaz <john.diaz@stardata.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: A/B rollout status — completed rollback and exec summary

John — rollback complete and short executive summary below.

What we did:
- Paused variant B canary at 25% and routed all affected traffic back to variant A (v2.0-q8) at 10:03 PT. No customer job interruption — requests drained gracefully.
- Monitored metrics: p95 and p99 returned to baseline within ~7 minutes after the routing change. See Datadog link: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/12345678/p95-p99-stardata
- Engineering notes: quantized variant v2.1-q4f triggers a slower attention kernel under long-sequence loads leading to queue growth. Team will investigate a kernel fix and run a synthetic pass before any re-rollout.

Next steps:
1) Marcus to run detailed profile and open an internal bug with kernel trace (JIRA-OPS-1127).
2) Product (Lauren) will coordinate a new canary plan: smaller increments, route-aware throttling, and extended blackbox tests against >1024 token flows.
3) Sales (Ben) to draft a customer-facing note and offer 1-week usage credit for affected workloads if needed.

Attached: rollback-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook checklist), dd-profiles-20290429.txt, canary-metrics-variantB-20290429.csv

We will follow up with a postmortem once the investigation completes. Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
